solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gold added to state carriage

indicators.note: added to says the gold piece is tacked on after the state piece

parts.note: a state is a country, a land
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Gilding is applied to a ceremonial state coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding hood, a type of carriage.

clue.text: Women who saw wartime service in the field

definitions.text: Women who saw wartime service in the field

parts.words: Women who saw wartime service in the field
parts.note: in the field sounds like on the battlefield, but it means literally working on farm fields

explanation.surface: Women who served at the front during the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the field' suggests combat; Britain's Women's Land Army worked on farms in both world wars.
explanation.definitionFit: The Women's Land Army recruited British women to farm labour during the world wars.

clue.text: Ships of the fleet heel over

definitions.text: Ships of the fleet heel over

parts.note: a navy is a country's fleet of warships
to list is to lean or tilt to one side, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Vessels of the fleet lean over in a swell.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the official register of a navy's ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The Navy List is the official published register of a navy's vessels and officers.

clue.text: Terrible acting, so lacking in belief

indicators.note: terrible acting is ham work, so these letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: The acting was so awful the audience could not believe in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic holds that God's existence cannot be known, withholding religious conviction.

clue.text: Breakfast ingredient fresh from fridge, for example

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made anew, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Something for breakfast taken straight out of the fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' is the anagram signal working on FRIDGE plus EG together.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried egg is a staple item of a cooked morning meal.

clue.text: One often out on the tiles

definitions.text: One often out on the tiles

parts.words: One often out on the tiles
parts.note: out on the tiles is an idiom for partying, but here it means literally up on roof tiles

explanation.surface: A party-lover who is frequently out on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out on the tiles' is British slang for a night of carousing; here it is literal work up on a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofer works on top of buildings, laying and repairing slates and tiles.

clue.text: It goes amiss to be a selfish type

indicators.note: amiss means wrongly placed, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Things go wrong when someone behaves selfishly.
explanation.definitionFit: An egoist is a person who puts their own interests first, a self-centred person.

clue.text: Head left student to get a good job

indicators.note: Head left means the leading letter of the student word goes away

parts.note: a learner is a student

explanation.surface: A headteacher left a pupil to land a fine position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head left' reads as a headteacher departing; it means the word loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nice little earner is British slang for a lucrative job or money-spinner.

clue.text: Regiment in the van

definitions.meaning: elite British army regiments, such as the Grenadiers
railway ... ride in the ... van at the back of a British train; also, ... are those in the vanguard

explanation.surface: A regiment travelling at the front of the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' reads as the vanguard of troops; it is also the guard's van, the British name for a train's brake carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Guards are famous household regiments and also train officials who ride in the guard's van.

clue.text: Nave tidied up following a number of days of prayer

indicators.note: following puts the rearranged letters after the number piece

parts.note: No. is the usual abbreviation for number

indicators.note: tidied up means the letters are rearranged into order

explanation.surface: A church nave is tidied after a series of days of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A novena is a Catholic devotion of prayers said over nine successive days.

clue.text: Exclusive neighbourhood

parts.note: exclusive reads as posh, but it means a district from which people are excluded

explanation.surface: An upmarket, select part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exclusive' usually means fashionable and select; here it means shutting people out, as police or troops do.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-go area is a district where outsiders or authorities are barred or dare not enter.

clue.text: Where the cobbler may be found, after some delay

definitions.text: Where the cobbler may be found
definitions.meaning: a shoemaker works at his last, the foot-shaped block for shaping shoes
finally, eventually, when one has waited long

explanation.surface: Finding the shoe-mender took a while.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is a cobbler's foot-shaped form, so the cobbler is found working at it; the phrase also means finally.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means finally, eventually, and literally places a shoemaker beside his foot-shaped mould.

clue.text: Support for one who is lying

definitions.text: Support for one who is lying

parts.words: Support for one who is lying
parts.note: lying suggests telling untruths, but it means lying down in bed

explanation.surface: Backing given to someone who tells fibs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' tempts toward dishonesty; it is reclining, and the frame holds up the sleeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedstead is the framework of a bed that holds up a person resting on it.

clue.text: Risk taking a chance about meat on the bone

indicators.note: about means the gamble word surrounds the risk word

parts.note: a bet is a chance taken, a gamble

explanation.surface: Gambling over a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is a cut of beef from the breast, often sold bone-in.

clue.text: Slip of a girl losing head on river

indicators.note: on, in an across entry, places the river letter after the other piece
losing head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: her refers to a girl or woman
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A young girl stumbles at the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip of a girl' looks like one phrase meaning a slim young woman; 'Slip' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, and a slip is a small mistake, both as verbs.

clue.text: Section of the army stick together in a mysterious way

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A unit of soldiers sticks together in some inexplicable way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Section' looks like a military unit, fitting 'army', but it signals a run of letters lifted from inside 'army stick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystic describes something spiritually obscure, beyond ordinary understanding, joined to the unseen.

clue.text: One over the eight

parts.note: one over the eight is British slang for slightly drunk, but here it is the person in charge of eight rowers

explanation.surface: Someone who has had one drink too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is a British idiom for tipsy; in rowing an eight is a crew of eight oarsmen, steered by one person.
explanation.definitionFit: The coxswain steers and commands a rowing eight, so is set over its crew.

clue.text: Drink with a bite

definitions.meaning: a small measure of spirits, a tot
a small sharp pinch with the teeth

explanation.surface: A drink with some kick to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a dram of liquor and a quick nibble or pinch.

clue.text: Primrose makes a neat petticoat

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a single neat is a cow
a slip is a woman's petticoat or underskirt

explanation.surface: A primrose-coloured fabric makes a tidy underskirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' reads as tidy, but it is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a wild flower of the genus Primula, so a kind of primrose.

clue.text: Narrow defile left for getting from one country to another

definitions.text: for getting from one country to another

parts.note: a pass is a narrow route through mountains, a defile
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A mountain pass left open for crossing a border.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the travel document needed to cross international borders.

clue.text: Partner in team given the boot

parts.note: a side is a team
giving someone the boot is a kick

explanation.surface: A teammate is sacked from the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given the boot' reads as dismissed; the boot is a kick.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a close companion or assistant, someone's partner in exploits.

clue.text: Dogs sulk with cats around

indicators.note: around says the whips word encloses the sulk word

parts.note: a cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, so cats are whips
a pet is a fit of sulking, as in in a pet

explanation.surface: Dogs mope when cats are about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cats' looks like the dogs' natural foes; it is short for cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: Whippets are slender, fast racing dogs related to greyhounds.

clue.text: Fairly average kind of district

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
the suffix -ish means fairly or somewhat

explanation.surface: An area that is mediocre, middling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairly average' becomes average-ish, so the average piece comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is a small local district with its own church, or a civil administrative unit.

clue.text: A disposition of arms

parts.note: disposition of arms sounds like deploying weapons, but it is how the limbs are placed

explanation.surface: A deployment of weaponry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' reads as weapons; it means the limbs, hands on hips and elbows out.
explanation.definitionFit: Akimbo describes standing with hands on hips and elbows turned outward.

clue.text: The ego-trip of a German writer

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A German author's self-indulgent jaunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ego-trip' reads as vanity; 'trip' is the anagram signal on THE EGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, author of Faust, is the most celebrated German man of letters.

clue.text: Nut-cases?

parts.note: nut-cases suggests madmen, but it reads as cases for nuts, nut being slang for the head

explanation.surface: Lunatics?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' is slang for the head, so the cases that hold heads are the bony craniums.
explanation.definitionFit: The cranium encases the head, which slang calls the nut.

clue.text: Comb manufacturer

parts.note: comb suggests a hair comb, but it is the honeycomb of wax cells

explanation.surface: A firm that makes hair combs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comb' points to grooming; the maker builds honeycomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeybees secrete wax and build the honeycomb in the hive.

clue.text: Footsore British group of workers

parts.note: a union is an organised body of workers

explanation.surface: A weary-footed British trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Footsore' reads as tired feet; it is taken as a sore on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunion is a painful swelling on the joint of the big toe, a sore on the foot.

clue.text: A stunning performance

parts.note: stunning sounds like amazing, but it is literally a blow that leaves someone senseless

explanation.surface: A brilliant, dazzling show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunning' means superb in the surface, and literally dazing in the boxing reading; the word means both.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout is both a sensational success and a blow rendering a boxer unconscious.

clue.text: As yet unalarmed?

parts.note: unalarmed sounds like calm, but it means the alarm clock has not yet gone off

explanation.surface: Someone who has not yet become worried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unalarmed' means not frightened in the surface; here it means not yet woken by an alarm clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping has not yet been roused by the alarm clock ringing.

clue.text: Encountered everyone in charge of minerals

parts.note: met means encountered
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Meeting everybody who runs the mining resources.
explanation.definitionFit: Metallic describes things made of or relating to metals, which are mineral substances.

clue.text: I get nothing to eat from the medicine chest

parts.note: O, the round zero figure, stands for nothing
to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Someone gets no food, only things from the medicine cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tincture of this element was a standard antiseptic kept in household first-aid cupboards.

clue.text: After an order, is the worker showing respect?

indicators.note: After places the following pieces behind the order piece

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
the worker ant is a crossword standby for worker

explanation.surface: After being given a command, is the employee deferential?
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' reads as a command; it is the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant means deferential, making a bow or gesture of homage.

clue.text: Race bets

definitions.meaning: a horse race with prize money
sums of money wagered on an outcome

explanation.surface: Wagers placed on a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Stakes names a type of horse race and also the money risked in gambling.
